articles.headline: UP CEO confident rail merger application checks all the STB's boxes
articles.summary: Union Pacific CEO expressed confidence that the revised UP-Norfolk Southern merger application meets all requirements set by the Surface Transportation Board. The application has been resubmitted following earlier review. No timeline for STB action was specified in the report.

articles.headline: Target moves to elevate supply chain operations, inventory reliability
articles.summary: Target has identified supply chain improvement as a strategic priority, aiming to eliminate out-of-stock situations and reduce operational costs. The retailer is investing in supply chain operations to improve inventory reliability across its network. The initiative reflects ongoing efforts by major retailers to strengthen distribution and fulfillment capabilities.

articles.headline: DoJ indicts Chinese container makers on price-fixing charges
articles.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice has indicted four major Chinese shipping container manufacturers and seven individual executives on charges related to a global price-fixing conspiracy. The indictments target some of the world's largest box manufacturers. The action follows other U.S. measures against Chinese logistics and port equipment firms, including reciprocal port fees and tariffs.

articles.headline: Another CA truck crash and two dead kids on Highway 99
articles.summary: A Freightliner Cascadia operated by Amritsar Trans Inc., a five-truck carrier based in Manteca, California, rear-ended three vehicles on Highway 99 near Lodi on May 19, 2026, killing two young men. The driver fled the scene on foot following the collision. The carrier is described as operating within a broader web of compliance concerns.

articles.headline: Rail on a roll as ag, metals, chemicals lead traffic
articles.summary: U.S. rail freight volumes posted another positive week, with seven out of 10 commodity categories showing year-over-year improvement. Agricultural products, metals, and chemicals led traffic gains during the reporting period. The data reflects continued broad-based strength in rail freight demand.

articles.headline: 79 ELDs revoked since January. 12 more just hit the list.
articles.summary: The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration removed 12 additional electronic logging devices from its registered device list, bringing the total number of revocations to 79 since January 2025. The pace of removals is outstripping the rate at which new devices are being added to the registry. The trend raises questions about the agency's longer-term direction on ELD oversight.

articles.headline: RXO sees TL spot market surge further in Q2
articles.summary: Freight broker RXO reported better-than-expected spot market conditions in the second quarter of 2026, with truckload spot rates surging beyond earlier projections. The company indicated that Q2 trends are tracking above internal forecasts. The development signals improving freight demand conditions in the broader truckload market.

articles.headline: Evolution of ocean capacity linked to varied dynamics of trade needs
articles.summary: The alignment between ocean freight demand and vessel capacity supply varies significantly across individual trade lanes, according to an analysis by Jeremy Masters. These dynamics carry different consequences for the newbuild, second-hand, and charter vessel markets. The piece examines how trade-lane-specific conditions are shaping carrier capacity deployment decisions.

articles.headline: US move against container makers is latest entry in logistics battle with China
articles.summary: The Justice Department's indictments against four major Chinese container manufacturers are the latest in a series of U.S. actions targeting Chinese dominance in logistics infrastructure. Prior measures have included reciprocal port fees and tariffs on China-made port equipment. The indictments allege a global price-fixing conspiracy involving the box manufacturers and multiple executives.

articles.headline: Zim reports Q1 loss, with bunker impact expected to worsen in Q2
articles.summary: Zim Integrated Shipping Services reported a net loss in the first quarter of 2026, with CEO Eli Glickman citing war-driven oil price increases as a significant drag on results. Glickman warned that bunker fuel costs are expected to weigh more heavily on the company's financials in the second quarter. Zim declined to offer earnings guidance, citing the pending merger with Hapag-Lloyd.

articles.headline: Spot rate surge may signal early peak season on trans-Pacific
articles.summary: Trans-Pacific spot and FAK freight rates have surged, with some analysts suggesting the move may indicate an earlier-than-usual peak shipping season. The strength of any peak remains uncertain, with blank sailings, fuel-linked surcharges, and the annual service contract changeover all contributing to upward rate pressure. The underlying demand drivers have not been fully established.

articles.headline: Matson reports air-to-ocean freight conversions amid Iran war
articles.summary: U.S.-based ocean carrier Matson reported observing a shift in shipper behavior, with customers converting air freight shipments to ocean freight amid the ongoing conflict involving Iran. The carrier linked the trend to disruptions and cost pressures affecting air cargo routing. Matson's comments provide insight into how the Iran conflict is influencing shipper modal decisions.

articles.headline: Danone to close plant-based dairy facility in New Jersey
articles.summary: Danone announced plans to close a plant-based dairy manufacturing facility in New Jersey that produces its Silk and So Delicious brands. The closure represents a reduction in the company's North American manufacturing footprint for plant-based products. Danone has not disclosed the number of workers affected or a specific timeline for the shutdown.

articles.headline: EU lawmakers back US trade pact with built-in safeguards
articles.summary: The European Parliament has voted to support a trade agreement with the United States that includes built-in safeguard mechanisms. The pact is designed to govern tariff and trade flow conditions between the EU and the U.S. Specific terms of the safeguards and the timeline for ratification were not detailed in the available description.

articles.headline: Muted peak season expected as ocean shippers delay contract signing
articles.summary: Ocean shippers are delaying the signing of annual contracts amid market uncertainty, contributing to expectations of a muted peak shipping season. The hesitation reflects broader uncertainty about trade volumes and freight rate direction heading into the second half of the year. The delay in contract commitments signals that shippers are opting for flexibility over locked-in rates as conditions remain unpredictable.

articles.headline: Up, up, and (put)away
articles.summary: Warehouses and distribution centers are facing sustained pressure to accommodate growing inventory volumes, more SKUs, higher order counts, and increased shipments. Expanding existing building footprints is not always feasible, prompting operators to explore alternative strategies for capacity growth. The article examines approaches facilities are taking to maximize throughput within constrained physical footprints.

articles.headline: Insurance cost increases outpace consumer inflation, trucking industry report shows
articles.summary: Trucking industry insurance premiums are rising at a rate more than five percentage points above consumer inflation, according to a new report from the American Transportation Research Institute (ATRI). The report, focused on trucking industry costs, highlights insurance as a growing financial burden for carriers. ATRI's data underscores the widening gap between general inflation and sector-specific cost pressures facing motor carriers.

articles.headline: LA County brings Palisades, Eaton fire recovery efforts under one roof with new agency
articles.summary: The Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors voted Tuesday to establish a new agency dedicated to coordinating long-term recovery efforts from the January 2025 Palisades and Eaton fires. The agency is designed to streamline the rebuilding process by consolidating bureaucratic functions that have historically slowed post-disaster reconstruction. The move formalizes the county's recovery apparatus as rebuilding efforts in affected communities continue.

articles.headline: LA County's post-fire rent gouging ban goes up in smoke
articles.summary: The Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors failed to secure the votes necessary to extend an emergency anti-price gouging ban on rents that was enacted following the January 2025 wildfires. The expiration of the ban will give landlords greater pricing flexibility in a rental market still affected by fire-related displacement. The vote outcome means tenant protections tied to the disaster declaration will lapse.

articles.headline: Onni's $400M loan finds itself in special servicing again
articles.summary: Onni Group's $408 million loan secured by Wilshire Courtyard has been transferred to special servicing, according to Morningstar Credit. The approximately one-million-square-foot Miracle Mile office complex is located at 5700 to 5750 Wilshire Boulevard in Los Angeles. Onni currently owes approximately $384 million on the loan, and the servicer has been engaged to manage the distressed debt situation.

articles.headline: Fed Minutes Show More Officials Warned of Rate-Hike Scenario
articles.summary: A majority of Federal Reserve officials warned the central bank would likely need to consider raising interest rates if inflation continued to run persistently above their 2% target, according to minutes of the April 28–29 FOMC meeting. Many officials called for the Fed to drop its easing bias and signal its next move could be a rate increase. The April meeting featured four dissenting votes — the most since 1992 — with three members objecting to language implying future cuts remain the base case. The minutes were released as incoming Fed Chair Kevin Warsh prepares to be sworn in, and markets are now pricing roughly a 39% probability of a rate hike by year-end.

articles.headline: Bond Yield Spike: What It Means for Economies and Markets
articles.summary: A prolonged period of elevated long-term bond yields is ramping up borrowing costs around the world, as investors demand more compensation for holding government debt following the Iran war's ignition of fresh inflation fears. Yields on 30-year US Treasuries have risen above 5% to the highest since 2007, while equivalent UK debt is yielding the most in almost three decades. The rate on 20-year Japanese bonds is the highest since 1996. The global bond selloff reflects compounding concerns over public debt levels, central bank rate paths, and sustained energy-driven inflation.

articles.headline: Bond Yields Are Rising for Reasons Both Benign and Concerning
articles.summary: Bloomberg Opinion columnist and former New York Fed President Bill Dudley writes that yields on 10-year Treasury notes have risen nearly half a percentage point to just under 4.70% this week — the highest since January 2025. Dudley identifies three cyclical drivers: stronger-than-anticipated economic growth, sustained consumer spending despite energy and tariff shocks, and a surge in business investment led by AI infrastructure buildout. Expectations for monetary policy have shifted from rate cuts to potential increases, with prevailing market wisdom now pointing toward tightening rather than easing.

articles.headline: Stock Market Today: Dow, S&P Live Updates for May 21
articles.summary: A US–Iran standoff over key peace deal terms lifted oil prices on May 21, dragging down stocks and bonds on concern that a prolonged Strait of Hormuz closure could worsen energy disruptions and fuel inflation. While Tehran said the latest Washington proposal had partly bridged the gap between the two sides, a report that Iran plans to retain its near-weapons-grade uranium was seen as a potential setback. The S&P 500 erased its week-to-date gain, and US crude topped $101 per barrel, driving Treasury yields higher on fears the Fed will be forced to raise rates.

articles.headline: Repeat After Me, Stocks Are Not an Effective Inflation Hedge
articles.summary: Bloomberg analysis reports that investors are piling into equities even as they anticipate rising inflation, a strategy Bloomberg argues is likely to backfire. Inflation is described as resurgent as the energy shock from the Iran war ripples through the global economy. The net percentage of respondents in Bank of America's Fund Manager Survey expecting higher inflation is back at its highest level since the pandemic. The piece urges investors to refocus on real economic quantities rather than nominal equity values.

articles.headline: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for May 21
articles.summary: Oil prices inched higher after plummeting on Wednesday, as President Trump said the US is in the "final stages" of negotiations with Iran. Brent crude was above $105 per barrel after sliding 5.6% the prior session, while West Texas Intermediate traded near $99. Trump's comments to reporters stoked hopes for a deal between Washington and Tehran that would see a near-term restart of energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Price volatility is directly tied to the status of peace negotiations and their potential effect on global oil supply.

articles.headline: Euro-Area Output Falls Sharply, Raising Risks for Growth and Inflation
articles.summary: Business activity in the euro area shrank at the quickest pace in 2½ years in May, adding to fears that the Iran war and accompanying surge in energy costs are dealing a severe blow to the economy. The Composite Purchasing Managers' Index compiled by S&P Global fell to 47.5 in May from 48.8 in April, holding below the 50-point expansion threshold for a second consecutive month. Bloomberg survey analysts had anticipated an unchanged reading. The sharper-than-expected contraction compounds inflation concerns and raises questions about the ECB's monetary policy path.

articles.headline: ICE Raids Did Lasting Damage to American Businesses
articles.summary: Bloomberg's data-driven investigation finds that foot traffic and sales in a Charlotte, North Carolina immigrant business corridor remain depressed six months after the Department of Homeland Security's Operation Charlotte's Web deportation raids in November 2025. The analysis documents measurable, persistent economic decline in a one-mile stretch of Central Avenue filled with immigrant-owned businesses. The report is part of Bloomberg's broader coverage of the microeconomic consequences of federal immigration enforcement for bellwether firms. The findings illustrate how enforcement operations are creating lasting demand destruction in specific labor and consumer markets relevant to industrial tenant operating conditions.

articles.headline: Anthropic Revenue Surges, Set to Post First Profit
articles.summary: The Wall Street Journal was first to report that Anthropic has told investors it expects Q2 revenue of $10.9 billion — a 130% increase over Q1's $4.8 billion — which would surpass the company's total 2025 annual sales. The company projects an operating profit of $559 million for the June quarter, which would mark its first profitable quarter since founding in 2021. The figures were shared with investors as part of an ongoing funding round that could push Anthropic's valuation above OpenAI's. Anthropic does not expect sustained profitability throughout the full year due to substantial upcoming compute infrastructure spending.

articles.headline: Walmart Posts Strong Q1 Results But Cautious Guidance Rattles Investors
articles.summary: Walmart reported Q1 FY27 net sales of $175.7 billion, topping the $174.8 billion analyst consensus, with e-commerce sales up 26% globally and Walmart U.S. comparable sales growth of 4.1%. The company reported adjusted EPS of $0.66, matching Wall Street forecasts, with net income of $5.33 billion. Executives left full-year FY27 guidance unchanged and warned that persistently high fuel costs — driven by the U.S.-Iran war's disruption of Strait of Hormuz tanker traffic — would increasingly pressure store prices and consumer spending in Q2. Walmart's stock fell approximately 7% on the day as investors reacted to the flat guidance and fuel cost warnings.

articles.headline: SpaceX Is Aiming to Go Public on June 12, Setting the Stage for What Is Expected to Be the Biggest IPO of All Time
articles.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that SpaceX is targeting a June 12 Nasdaq listing under the ticker SPCX, with pricing expected June 11 and a formal roadshow beginning June 4. The company is seeking to raise approximately $75 billion at a valuation of roughly $1.75 trillion, which would make it the largest IPO on record, surpassing Saudi Aramco's 2019 debut. Goldman Sachs is leading the offering alongside Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, Citigroup, and JPMorgan. The S-1 prospectus, filed with the SEC in April, discloses combined SpaceX-xAI 2025 revenue of $18.67 billion following SpaceX's all-stock acquisition of xAI in February 2026.

articles.headline: West Marine Files for Chapter 11 Bankruptcy, Plans to Rationalize Its Store Footprint
articles.summary: West Marine, the largest U.S. boating and marine supplies retailer, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware on May 17, 2026. The company secured a Restructuring Support Agreement backed by 96.2% of its term loan lenders, 100% of its FILO lenders, and 93.9% of equity holders, with secured lenders also committing to new exit financing. West Marine's approximately 200 retail locations across 34 states and Puerto Rico will remain open during the restructuring, with the company stating it intends to 'optimize operations and rationalize its footprint.' The company's largest unsecured creditor is Garmin International at $8.57 million, followed by distribution logistics company Virtual Supply Inc. at $5.8 million. Portage Point Partners is serving as investment banker.

articles.headline: CoStar World News for May 21
articles.summary: CoStar's daily international news digest for May 21 covers global CRE investment trends. French non-traded REIT fundraising increased 10% year-over-year to €1.2 billion in Q1 2026, with diversified funds accounting for 72% of inflows; logistics and industrial captured 3% of total investment inflows. The roundup also includes German residential debt issuance, Toronto investment market data showing a $3.4 billion year-over-year gain in aggregate investment volume, and retail market analysis from a JLL report presented at ICSC's Las Vegas conference.

articles.headline: How The Wonderful Logistics Center Is Transforming California's Central Valley
articles.summary: The Wonderful Company's Wonderful Logistics Center in Shafter, California is a 2,000-acre, fully entitled and master-planned logistics development featuring more than 17 million square feet of space currently in operation, with over 10,000 careers created since opening. Wonderful Real Estate, a division of The Wonderful Company, is developing three business parks totaling 1,865 acres in California's Central Valley, with multiple properties already leased or purchased by Fortune 500 companies. The article notes the U.S. industrial market posted 40 million square feet of net absorption in Q1 2026, its best quarterly result in three years, with tenants increasingly seeking newer warehouse products capable of supporting automation, AI systems, and higher power requirements. The article was produced in collaboration with BisNow's Studio B content studio.

articles.headline: US-China Tariff Rates: Where Things Stand as of May 20, 2026
articles.summary: China and the US appear to have agreed on terms for restoration of US tariffs on Chinese goods through Section 301 investigations, following the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing, though no extension to the one-year trade truce through November 2026 has been finalized. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Reuters on May 19 that he believes China will accept restoration of prior tariff rates 'as long as they don't go higher,' with the two Section 301 investigations set to conclude this summer. The effective tariff rate on many Chinese goods shipped to the US remains close to 30%, still the highest of any country, reflecting a 15% global tariff in effect since February 24, 2026 plus surviving Section 232 and Section 301 duties. Section 301 tariff exclusions for 178 products have been extended until November 10, 2026.

articles.headline: Motor Carriers Game Out USMCA Futures Ahead of July 1 Deadline
articles.summary: Motor carriers across North America are adjusting investment and network decisions as the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement enters its first mandatory review ahead of a July 1 milestone, with initial US-Mexico talks starting the week of May 25. Carriers say prolonged uncertainty, not border disruption, risks chilling investment and capacity planning in an already fragile freight market. The three countries must decide by July 1 whether to extend USMCA for 16 years or begin annual reviews that could lead to expiration by 2036. TFI International Chairman Alain Bédard told analysts the uncertainty is too high to make major capital commitments until the agreement's future is clarified.

articles.headline: AAR slams "hypocrisy" as Trump-backed rail safety measure is included in transportation funding bill
articles.summary: The Association of American Railroads has criticized the inclusion of the Railway Safety Act in surface transportation funding legislation, calling the move hypocritical. The bill, which railroads have long opposed, gained traction after receiving backing from President Trump. The AAR's objection centers on the legislation being attached to broader surface transportation funding measures.

articles.headline: Broker liability ruling: Carriers, brokers, analysts weigh in
articles.summary: Industry participants are weighing in on the Supreme Court's landmark ruling on freight broker liability, with analysts and carriers largely viewing asset-based carriers as the primary beneficiaries. The ruling drew responses from brokers, carriers, and analysts across the freight industry. The decision is expected to reshape liability responsibilities within the freight brokerage sector.

articles.headline: Georgia ports volumes hit by higher costs, softer market
articles.summary: The Georgia Ports Authority reported that the Port of Savannah's latest container volume figures reflected the impact of higher operating costs and a softer market environment. The authority attributed the weaker results directly to those two factors in its release of the figures. The Port of Savannah is one of the largest container ports in the United States.

articles.headline: Walmart credits fast delivery, third-party marketplace for revenue gains
articles.summary: Walmart reported a 26% gain in e-commerce sales during the first quarter, attributing the growth to faster delivery speeds enabled by its supply chain system and expansion of its third-party marketplace. The retailer said increased delivery convenience was a key driver of the online sales performance. Walmart's logistics infrastructure has been a central component of its strategy to compete in the e-commerce sector.

articles.headline: ILWU chief slams 'foreign shipping companies' ahead of contract expiration
articles.summary: International Longshore and Warehouse Union President Bobby Olvera delivered a speech criticizing foreign shipping companies ahead of the ILWU's longshore contract expiration in 2028. Olvera's remarks were characterized as a warning shot directed at employers and cargo owners. The speech signals potential labor tension at West Coast ports as the contract deadline approaches.

articles.headline: 'Dummy permits' could overcome last-mile snafus for project cargoes
articles.summary: Project shippers in the U.S. are being encouraged to use so-called "dummy permits" to test bridge strength and state permitting feasibility up to a year before major cargo moves. The approach is intended to help shippers identify and resolve last-mile transportation obstacles in advance of actual shipments. The strategy addresses ongoing challenges in routing heavy or oversized project cargo through domestic infrastructure.

articles.headline: AvalonBay, Equity Residential Merging to Form $69B Multifamily Giant
articles.summary: AvalonBay Communities and Equity Residential announced a merger that will create a combined entity with a total enterprise value of approximately $69 billion, making it one of the largest real estate companies in the United States. The two firms rank among the country's largest multifamily owners. The combined company will hold a substantial national apartment portfolio spanning multiple major markets.

articles.headline: Treasury Yields Fall as Hopes Rise for End to US-Iran War
articles.summary: US government bonds reversed an earlier decline to post gains as oil retreated on hopes that an agreement to end the US-Iran war will be reached soon. Treasury yields across maturities fell as much as three basis points intraday, with the 10-year note yield approaching 4.55% and extending its decline from a recent high above 4.68% — the highest since January 2025. The move tracked a drop in crude oil prices tied to diplomatic signals on a potential Strait of Hormuz reopening.

articles.headline: War Weighs on Global Growth With Inflation Worries Intensifying
articles.summary: The global economy is showing signs of waning momentum and mounting inflation pressures during its third month of a war-induced energy crunch. Purchasing manager surveys from Australia to Europe pointed to an intensifying ordeal for manufacturing and services companies in May. Factory activity as measured by S&P Global either slowed or contracted across all indexes released on Thursday, with the exception of the UK.

articles.headline: Rising Recession Risk on Shut Strait of Hormuz: Evening Briefing Americas
articles.summary: Energy consultancy Rapidan Energy Group warned that continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz through summer raises the risk of a recession that may rival the global financial crisis. It has been nearly three months since the start of the Iran war and concomitant blockage of the strait, with energy prices spiking globally. Rapidan's warning centers on the August deadline as a critical threshold for when market conditions could deteriorate sharply.

articles.headline: AvalonBay, Equity Residential Said to Near Mega-REIT Tie Up
articles.summary: AvalonBay Communities Inc. and Equity Residential are nearing a deal that would combine two of the largest apartment REITs by market value, according to people familiar with the matter. The terms under discussion would provide 2.793 shares of Equity Residential common stock — which closed Wednesday at $66.28 per share — for each share of AvalonBay stock. A transaction could be announced as soon as Thursday, according to the sources, who asked not to be identified as the information is confidential.

articles.headline: 5 Manufacturers Announcing New US Production Facilities
articles.summary: IndustryWeek compiled five recent U.S. manufacturing facility announcements, including Novartis confirming a new 56,200-square-foot active pharmaceutical ingredients facility in Morrisville, North Carolina, as part of its $23 billion U.S. manufacturing investment commitment. Whirlpool Corp. announced a $60 million investment to convert an existing Perrysburg, Ohio building—previously used for solar panel manufacturing—into its 11th U.S. factory, expected to produce appliance components and create 100 to 150 jobs. Additional manufacturers with new domestic facility investments were also profiled in the roundup, reflecting the ongoing trend of companies broadening U.S. production footprints.

articles.headline: State of Freight 5 takeaways: Montgomery talk; short-term strength
articles.summary: FreightWaves' monthly State of Freight webinar highlighted fallout from the Montgomery case as a key discussion topic among freight industry participants. The webinar also identified short-term strength in freight market conditions. The Montgomery case was described as a subject generating notable industry attention at the time of the event.

articles.headline: Freight Fraud Has Gone Corporate
articles.summary: Freight fraud incidents are climbing by double digits year over year, according to analysis from Reliance Partners. The report details how freight fraud has evolved in structure and sophistication, taking on more organized, corporate characteristics. Reliance Partners also outlined recommended countermeasures for carriers and brokers facing the escalating threat.

articles.headline: OmniTrax tabs Hoskins to lead transload
articles.summary: OmniTRAX has appointed Hoskins as Vice President of Transload to lead expansion efforts across its network. The appointment is tied to a broader network-wide transload growth strategy at the short-line railroad operator. No further financial terms or timeline details were disclosed in the announcement.

articles.headline: CU Lines' network expansion gives fresh capacity influx into Middle East trades
articles.summary: Shanghai-based carrier CU Lines has launched two new services connecting Asia to the Middle East, adding fresh capacity to the Persian Gulf trade corridor. The expansion comes amid strong demand growth in the region and ongoing disruptions to mainline services on other routes. The new services are positioned to capture capacity demand described as showing strong growth signals in Middle East trades.

articles.headline: Top CBRE Researcher Ebere Anokute: E-Commerce's Impact Is 'Overblown'
articles.summary: CBRE researcher Ebere Anokute argues that the impact of e-commerce on commercial real estate has been overstated, according to a Commercial Observer interview. Anokute notes that macroeconomic factors including inflation, interest rates, and employment trends are complicating the read on where the retail sector sits in the current cycle. The comments reflect a broader reassessment of e-commerce's role as the primary driver of industrial and retail real estate demand dynamics.

articles.headline: Hormuz Closure Threatens Recession Rivaling 2008, Rapidan Says
articles.summary: A closure of the Strait of Hormuz through August raises the risk of an economic downturn approaching the scale of the 2008 Great Recession, according to Rapidan Energy Group analysis reported by Bloomberg. Rapidan's base case assumes the waterway reopens in July, resulting in an average oil demand reduction of 2.6 million barrels a day and benchmark Brent crude peaking near $130 a barrel over the summer. A more pessimistic scenario extending the closure through August would cause the oil supply deficit to grow to 6 billion barrels per day in Q3. The strait has been largely closed to non-Iranian shipping since the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in late February.

articles.headline: U.S. to Award $2 Billion to Quantum Computing Firms, Take Equity Stakes
articles.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported, citing the Commerce Department, that the Trump administration is awarding $2 billion in grants to nine quantum-computing companies in deals that include U.S. government equity stakes. IBM is the largest recipient at $1 billion and will use the CHIPS Act funding to establish Anderon, described as America's first dedicated quantum chip manufacturing facility in Albany, New York. GlobalFoundries is set to receive $375 million, while D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion are each expected to receive approximately $100 million. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick confirmed the deals; shares of quantum companies surged 7% to 30% on the news.

articles.headline: A New ELFA Survey Shows Equipment Finance Leaders Feeling Better About the Market After a Weaker April
articles.summary: The Equipment Leasing & Finance Association (ELFA) released its May 2026 Monthly Confidence Index for the Equipment Finance Industry, showing confidence rose to 59.9 from 54.6 in April. When assessing the next four months, 27.3% of executives believe business conditions will improve, up from 11.8% in April, while those expecting conditions to worsen fell to 9.1% from 29.4%. Demand for leases and loans to fund capital expenditures is expected to increase by 26.1% of respondents, up from 10.5% in April. The index provides a qualitative assessment from key executives in the $1.3 trillion equipment finance industry.

articles.headline: ITS Logistics May Supply Chain Report: Broker Liability Ruling and Inventory Replenishment Collide with Most Expensive Freight Market in Years
articles.summary: ITS Logistics released its May Supply Chain Report warning that capacity contraction, record transportation prices, and escalating parcel surcharges are squeezing shipper margins as restocking demand accelerates. CPI rose 3.8% year-over-year in April 2026, with energy prices from Strait of Hormuz disruptions pushing diesel more than $2 per gallon above last year's rates. The Logistics Managers' Index posted Transportation Price levels of 95.0 — the highest ever recorded — and dry van and reefer linehaul spot rates climbed more than 20% above the five-year average in mid-May. Capacity shortages are reported throughout key corridors as produce season continues.

articles.headline: Weekly Freight Report: May 21, 2026 — Hormuz Toll Talks, Peak Season Surcharges, China Tariff Floor Signals
articles.summary: Iran is in talks with Oman to formalize a permanent toll system for vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, with traffic collapsing from 135 ships per day pre-war to roughly 26 over a recent 48-hour window. Oil is hovering near $100 a barrel and pump prices have climbed above $4.55 a gallon — the highest since 2022 — with fuel surcharges baked into ocean and trucking quotes. Trans-Pacific spot rates have climbed roughly $1,000 per FEU since the Iran war began in late February, sitting at approximately $2,800 per FEU to the West Coast and $4,300 per FEU to the East Coast. Ocean Network Express filed a $2,000 per FEU peak season surcharge on eastbound trans-Pacific cargo effective June 1, with other carriers expected to follow.

articles.headline: WSI's Warehouse Wire: May 21, 2026 — USMCA Review, CVSA Roadcheck Fallout, and Manufacturing Trade Stakes
articles.summary: WSI's weekly roundup highlights a new National Association of Manufacturers report stating that U.S. goods exports to Canada and Mexico directly support 2 million American jobs, with 71% of imports from Canada and 64% from Mexico consisting of industrial materials, parts, components, or capital equipment used in further U.S. manufacturing. The May 12–14 CVSA International Roadcheck blitz resulted in 38,926 inspections, 69,446 violations, and 13,273 out-of-service orders, with carrier CSA BASIC scores expected to reflect the impact at the June 8 FMCSA Safety Measurement System update. FMCSA is also changing its DataQs challenge process beginning in mid-September, adding a three-stage independent review for denied challenges. Manufacturers cited in the NAM report said future investment plans depend on clear North American trade rules as USMCA talks intensify ahead of the July 1 deadline.

articles.headline: U.S. Indicts Four Chinese Container Manufacturers Alleging Pandemic-Era Price-Fixing Cartel
articles.summary: The U.S. Justice Department unsealed an indictment against four of the world's largest shipping container manufacturers — China International Marine Containers (CIMC), Dong Fang International Container, CXIC Group Containers, and Singamas Container Holdings — and seven executives, alleging they conspired to restrict output and fix prices of standard dry shipping containers from November 2019 through at least January 2024. The companies collectively manufacture approximately 95% of the world's standard unrefrigerated shipping containers, according to the DOJ. Prosecutors allege the conspiracy roughly doubled container prices between 2019 and 2021, with CIMC's profits soaring from $20 million in 2019 to $1.75 billion in 2021. One executive, Vick Ma of Singamas, was arrested in France in April and is awaiting extradition; six others remain at large. The case was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California.

articles.headline: Drewry World Container Index — May 21: Transpacific Rates Rise, ONE Files $2,000 PSS for June 1
articles.summary: Drewry's May 21 World Container Index shows freight rates from Shanghai to Los Angeles increased 1% to $3,385 per 40ft container, while Shanghai to New York grew 2% to $4,317 per 40ft container. Ocean Network Express (ONE) has announced a Peak Season Surcharge of $2,000 per 40ft container on Transpacific eastbound cargo, effective June 1, with CMA CGM announcing new FAK levels above current rates for Asia-Europe effective the same date. Seven blank sailings have been announced on the Transpacific for the coming week, tightening capacity. Drewry expects rates to increase further in coming weeks as early peak season trends emerge across East-West trade lanes, compounded by ongoing Middle East geopolitical tensions and elevated bunker costs.

articles.headline: Short line rail hits T&I truck benefits, costly safety mandates
articles.summary: A short line rail industry trade group responded to new surface transportation legislation, acknowledging some rail-positive provisions while expressing disappointment over inclusions that benefit heavier trucks and impose expensive safety mandates. The group said the truck-favorable measures could disadvantage short line operators competing for freight. The legislation's safety mandates were flagged as particularly costly for smaller rail carriers.

articles.headline: Sen. Cotton urges DOJ investigation of China-backed parcel carriers
articles.summary: Sen. Tom Cotton (R-AR) has called on the Department of Justice to investigate Chinese-controlled parcel delivery companies operating in the United States. Cotton alleges the companies receive heavy government subsidies that allow them to underprice domestic carriers. He also raised concerns that the firms may be sharing critical U.S. market data with Chinese interests.

articles.headline: Saia opens terminals in Pacific Northwest, Midwest
articles.summary: Less-than-truckload carrier Saia has expanded its national network by opening new service center terminals in Washington state and Indiana. The openings are part of the carrier's ongoing effort to broaden its geographic footprint across the country. Saia did not disclose the specific cities or the capacity of the new facilities.

articles.headline: Port Houston sees April cargo dip, expects rebound in May
articles.summary: Port Houston recorded its first container volume slowdown since early 2025 in April, according to port officials. Executives attributed the dip to broader market conditions but said improving May volumes indicate a quick recovery is underway. The port did not provide specific container volume figures for either month.

articles.headline: Robinson Fresh opens border cold-chain hub as Mexico produce imports grow
articles.summary: Robinson Fresh has opened a new cold-chain logistics center in South Texas to serve growing produce imports from Mexico. Company executives said the facility is designed to help customers manage increasingly complex cross-border supply chains. The move comes as Mexico produce import volumes have been expanding, increasing demand for temperature-controlled border infrastructure.

articles.headline: ATRI documents big jump in insurance premiums even as providers in the red
articles.summary: The American Transportation Research Institute (ATRI) has released a report documenting a significant spike in truck insurance premiums paid by carriers. The report notes the premium increases are occurring even as insurance providers themselves are operating at a loss. ATRI did not specify the exact percentage increase in premiums in the available description.

articles.headline: CMA CGM posts Q1 earnings decline amid volatile ocean trade
articles.summary: CMA CGM reported a sharp drop in net profit for the first quarter, with financials pressured by ongoing Middle East tensions, rising oil prices, and increasing operating costs. The carrier's results reflect a market roiled by geopolitical instability affecting key trade lanes. CMA CGM did not provide specific net profit figures in the available summary.

articles.headline: Demand rising on Asia-Europe ocean trade as July bunker hike looms
articles.summary: Volumes on the Asia-Europe ocean trade lane are rising as shippers brace for a significant bunker fuel cost increase set to take effect at the start of the third quarter. Contracts locked in when the Middle East conflict began included quarterly bunker fuel adjustments that carriers are now preparing to pass on to shippers in July. The looming surcharge is adding cost pressure to an already volatile trade environment.

articles.headline: Heavy-lift trade group lobbies USTR for relief from crane, trailer tariffs
articles.summary: A heavy-lift industry trade group is urging the U.S. Trade Representative to reduce tariffs on imported cranes and trailers, warning that domestic manufacturing capacity cannot be built up fast enough to compensate. Industry stakeholders cited a five-to-seven year lead time to develop domestic crane manufacturing, arguing the tariffs could cripple U.S. heavy-lift operations in the interim. The group did not specify which tariff schedule or rates are the subject of the lobbying effort.

articles.headline: J&J Snack Foods completes plant consolidation, turns to distribution
articles.summary: J&J Snack Foods has completed a manufacturing plant consolidation and is now shifting its operational focus toward distribution network improvements. The company did not disclose the specific number of facilities consolidated or the locations affected. The strategic pivot to distribution signals the company's next phase of supply chain optimization following the manufacturing restructuring.

articles.headline: Survey: Port leaders call for $6.7 billion cargo equipment spending
articles.summary: A survey of 25 senior port and terminal executives conducted by the National Association of Waterfront Employers found that U.S. ports require $6.7 billion in cargo equipment investment over the next five years to maintain efficiency and global competitiveness. Port leaders identified aging equipment as a key challenge to operational performance. The survey did not specify how the investment total was distributed across individual ports or equipment categories.

articles.headline: Printing company buys warehouse
articles.summary: InHouse Media Group, a printing company specializing in posters and music-industry art, has purchased an industrial facility in Chino for $3 million. The building, located at 14963 Sierra Bonita Lane near the 71 Freeway, totals 9,200 square feet. The transaction was reported by Progressive Real Estate Partners in Rancho Cucamonga.

articles.headline: Trump Tells Warsh to Do 'Own Thing' as Fed Chair Sworn In
articles.summary: Kevin Warsh was sworn in as the 17th chair of the Federal Reserve on Friday in a White House ceremony, administered by Supreme Court Associate Justice Clarence Thomas. President Trump stressed he wants Warsh to independently lead the Fed, seeking to downplay investor concern over political pressure on monetary policy decisions. Warsh, who has promised the biggest shakeup in decades at the central bank, takes the helm at a tense moment with soaring Treasury yields and persistent inflation driven by the Iran war energy shock. The White House swearing-in ceremony is the first of its kind since Alan Greenspan was sworn in under President Reagan in 1987.

articles.headline: Fed's Chris Waller Says Next Move as Likely to Be Interest Rate Hike as Cut
articles.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said Friday he supports making clear the central bank's next interest-rate move is just as likely to be an increase as a cut, citing the energy shock from the Iran war pushing up prices. Speaking at an economic forum in Germany, Waller said his current position is to be patient in holding rates but warned he would not rule out a future rate hike if inflation does not start to slow soon. Waller called for removing the FOMC's 'easing bias' language from its policy statement, stating 'inflation is not headed in the right direction' with the Fed's preferred inflation measure hitting 3.8% in April. His comments amplify the challenge facing incoming Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, who was sworn in just hours later.

articles.headline: Traders Bet Fed Under Warsh Will Hike Rates by December
articles.summary: Bond traders are now fully pricing in an interest-rate hike by the Federal Reserve this year, marking the first time such an outcome has been completely priced into interest-rate swaps. Traders boosted bets for higher rates on Friday after Fed Governor Christopher Waller said the central bank's next rate move is just as likely to be an increase as a cut. Interest-rate swaps imply the market sees the Fed's benchmark rate at least 25 basis points higher by end of 2026. The market shift occurred on the same day Kevin Warsh was sworn in as Fed Chair at the White House.

articles.headline: Stock Market Today: Dow, S&P Live Updates for May 22 — Iran Deal Hopes, Two-Year Yields Hit Highest Since February 2025
articles.summary: Hopes for a US-Iran deal turning a fragile ceasefire into lasting peace fueled Wall Street optimism on Friday, driving stocks toward their longest streak of weekly gains since 2023. The S&P 500 was set for an eighth straight week of gains following an 18% surge from war-fueled lows. Two-year Treasury yields hit their highest level since February 2025 after Fed Governor Christopher Waller supported making clear the next rate move is just as likely to be a raise as a cut. Money markets fully priced in a rate hike by December, and US oil hovered near $96 in a volatile session.

articles.headline: China Restricts Chemical Exports to US in Fentanyl Crackdown
articles.summary: China imposed new export controls on key chemical ingredients shipped to the US, Mexico, and Canada, framing the move as cooperation with Washington on curbing drug trafficking. Five government agencies now require special export licenses for three newly restricted compounds, according to an official announcement Friday. The targeted substances are primary building blocks used to manufacture illicit fentanyl. The restrictions signal continued evolution in US-China trade and regulatory coordination following the broader tariff truce.

articles.headline: China Will Have Rare Earths Leverage Over the US for a Long Time
articles.summary: Beijing's grip over the rare earths industry will persist for years, heavily influencing US-China ties and presenting long-term supply chain vulnerabilities for US manufacturers. The newsletter, written from Beijing, examines how China's dominance in rare earth refining and production continues to constrain Western industrial and defense supply chains despite significant new investment outside China. The report is subscriber-only and was published May 22, 2026.

articles.headline: China Launches Major Crackdown on Cross-Border Stock Trading
articles.summary: China launched an unprecedented campaign against illegal cross-border securities trading, threatening severe penalties against popular brokers and ordering non-compliant accounts to be liquidated within two years. Eight regulators issued a joint statement after onshore markets closed Friday, vowing a campaign against these trades, which sent US-listed Chinese stocks tumbling. The crackdown is aimed at stemming capital outflows from China. The action represents a significant escalation of China's controls over cross-border capital flows.

articles.headline: Saudi Wealth Fund Weighs Logistics Merger to Attract Global Investment
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund is considering consolidating its transport and supply-chain assets — including ports, rail, and shipping — into a single logistics entity to attract foreign investment and better serve the kingdom's trade hubs amid the Iran war disruption. The PIF has held early-stage talks on combining parts of its portfolio including the $8.3 billion National Shipping Company of Saudi Arabia and Saudi Global Ports, according to people familiar with the matter. The enlarged firm could evolve into a vehicle for multibillion-dollar investments and potentially include an IPO to bring in international investors. Discussions gained urgency after the ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz exposed vulnerabilities in Middle Eastern supply chains.

articles.headline: Gulf States Tell Ships Not to Use Iran's Strait of Hormuz Route
articles.summary: Five Middle Eastern countries — Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates — formally rejected Iran's establishment of the Persian Gulf Strait Authority to control transit through the Strait of Hormuz. In a letter to the International Maritime Organization distributed earlier this week, the five nations said commercial and merchant vessels should not engage with the PGSA or cross the waterway using Iran's designated route. The joint statement escalates the ongoing standoff over the strategically vital waterway, which has been largely closed to commercial shipping since the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran began on February 28. The letter signals a hardening of Gulf state opposition to Iran's claimed maritime authority.

articles.headline: Kevin Warsh Sworn In as Federal Reserve Chair at White House Ceremony
articles.summary: Kevin Warsh was sworn in as the 17th chair of the Federal Reserve at a White House ceremony on May 22, replacing Jerome Powell. President Trump stressed he wants Warsh to independently lead the central bank, seeking to downplay investor concern about political pressure on policy decisions. Warsh was confirmed by the Senate 55-45 on May 13 and has promised what he calls the biggest shakeup in decades at the Fed. Markets are pricing in a 97.2% chance of a rate hold at Warsh's first FOMC meeting, with rate cuts widely considered off the table amid persistent inflation driven by elevated oil prices.

articles.headline: What's Behind the Dangerous Brew for Bonds
articles.summary: WSJ chief economics commentator Greg Ip warned of a dangerous fundamental shift brewing in the bond market, tied to the combination of rising Treasury yields, elevated oil prices, and growing fiscal concerns surrounding the 'Big Beautiful' tax bill. The 30-year Treasury yield recently topped 5.19%, the highest level since 2007, while the 10-year yield rose to 4.62%. A weak 20-year Treasury auction showed demand at its lowest since February, with investors demanding higher yields to compensate for lending to the U.S. government. The FOMC's April minutes, released May 20, showed a majority of Fed officials warning that rate hikes may be necessary if inflation remains persistently above the 2% target.

articles.headline: Walmart Posts Strong Q1 FY27 Results but Distribution Fuel Costs Weigh on Operating Income
articles.summary: Walmart reported Q1 FY27 results on May 21, 2026, with U.S. comparable sales growing 4.1% and global e-commerce up 26%, but operating income was negatively affected by 250 basis points from higher fuel costs in distribution and fulfillment. The company issued Q2 FY27 guidance for net sales growth of 4% to 5% and adjusted operating income growth of 7% to 10% in constant currency, with adjusted EPS of $0.72 to $0.74. Walmart's full-year fiscal 2027 outlook remained unchanged from prior guidance. The company noted its investments in supply chain automation across U.S. distribution centers continue to scale.

articles.headline: April FOMC Minutes Show Officials Warned Rate Hike May Be Needed Amid Persistent Inflation
articles.summary: Minutes from the Federal Reserve's April 29 FOMC meeting, released May 20, showed that a majority of officials warned the central bank would likely need to consider raising interest rates if inflation continued to run persistently above the 2% target. The 8-4 vote to hold rates at 3.5%–3.75% marked the greatest internal dissent since October 1992, with four officials dissenting. Many participants called for the Fed to drop its easing bias, signaling that the next move could be a rate increase rather than a cut. The Fed cited elevated inflation driven in part by higher global energy prices linked to the Strait of Hormuz crisis as a key risk factor.

articles.headline: West Marine Files for Chapter 11 Bankruptcy in Delaware Court
articles.summary: West Marine, the largest boating and marine supplies retailer in the United States, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on May 17 in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware. The pre-arranged restructuring is backed by a Restructuring Support Agreement with 96.2% of term loan lenders, 100% of FILO lenders, and 93.9% of equity holders. The company's approximately 200 retail locations across 34 states and Puerto Rico remain open, with West Marine securing consensual use of cash collateral and new exit financing commitments from secured lenders. The filing follows a leveraged buyout debt load from a 2017 acquisition and ongoing trading difficulties through 2025 and into 2026.

articles.headline: AvalonBay and Equity Residential Agree to Merger, Creating $52 Billion Multifamily Giant
articles.summary: Apartment owners AvalonBay Communities and Equity Residential announced an all-stock merger of equals on May 20, 2026, creating a combined entity with a pro forma equity market capitalization of approximately $52 billion and an enterprise value of approximately $69 billion. The combined company will hold more than 180,000 rental apartments, with AvalonBay shareholders owning just over 51% of the combined entity. Both boards unanimously approved the merger agreement, and the combined company will operate under a new name to be announced prior to closing. Morgan Stanley and Centerview Partners advised Equity Residential, while the combined entity will be one of the largest multifamily REITs in the country.
